subject: zoology
question_text: Name two poisonous and two non-poisonous snakes found in South India.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.56, VSAQ 117). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. QUESTION WORDING: the book prints 'Name two poisonous and non poisonous snakes found in South India'; the card keeps the South India wording the paper asks and only repairs the grammar of the count. BOOK WORDING: the book prints 'Najanaja' and 'Viper russelli'; the accepted names are Naja naja and Vipera russelli, and the card uses those.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Poisonous snakes
steps.margin_note: Two names with the common name in brackets. Nothing else is needed for the mark.
lines: These snakes have poison fangs in the upper
steps.why: A poisonous snake is named by the fangs it carries, so writing the fang line once covers both examples.
common_mistakes: Writing only the common name. Give the scientific name; that is what is marked.
Naming the rat snake as poisonous. Ptyas is non-poisonous.
steps.memory_tip: Cobra and viper are the two poisonous names to keep; rat snake and pond snake are the safe pair.

steps.label: Non-poisonous snakes
steps.margin_note: Two names again. Four names in all carry the two marks.
lines: These snakes have no poison fangs. They kill
prey by holding or by coiling.
steps.why: The non-poisonous snakes are grouped by what they lack, so the fang line separates the two halves of the answer cleanly.
common_mistakes: Giving a python or a krait here. Bungarus (krait) is poisonous.
Writing two snakes in total. The question asks for two in EACH group.
steps.memory_tip: Two and two: cobra and viper on the poisonous side, rat snake and pond snake on the other.

insider_note: Four scientific names are the whole answer; spelling Naja naja and Vipera russelli correctly is worth more here than any description.
